0x00730102: Return the number of display heads for a subdevice; flags select the client's usable heads versus all heads. Input: subdevice and flags. Output: numHeads.
0x00730108: Detect connected displays using the requested detection flags (including cached/DDC paths). Input/output: display mask; also subdevice and retry time. This is connector discovery, not a GPU work submission.
0x0073010a: Read hotplug state for a subdevice, including lid-state flags and the hotplug-after-EDID display mask.
0x0073010c: Return the active display ID for a selected subdevice/head, with flags controlling client filtering.
0x00730122: Unresolved for Windows 580. Nouveau's historical r535 header assigns this number to GET_CONNECT_STATE with a 16-byte structure; Windows declares 8 bytes. r570 and OGKM 580 use 0x00730108 for connect state. The historical name is a candidate, not an established decoding of this call.
0x0073012c: Add or remove a display from VRR display information using subdevice, display ID and an addition/removal boolean. This updates display state rather than querying a generic capability mask.
0x00730250: Query connector metadata for a display: DDC partners, connector count and per-connector index/type/location, plus platform information. Inputs select subdevice/display and query flags.
0x00730280: Candidate HDCP-state query from newer OGKM 595: subdevice/display select the target and flags report protection state, including HDCP 2.2. Published and captured lengths both equal 12 bytes; this does not prove all 580 semantics identical.
0x00730282: Candidate HDCP control from newer OGKM 595: command/flags drive authentication or link/topology handling. The 595 parameter structure is 2608 bytes versus 2600 declared by Windows 580. Exact 580 field offsets and subcommand semantics remain unresolved; do not apply the newer structure verbatim.
0x0073028b: Query output-resource information for a display: resource index/type, protocol, dithering/location and connection/boot-state metadata. It describes the display routing hardware.
0x007302a4: Notify RM of a display transition using new-device mask, properties and start/end indication, allowing display changes to be coordinated.
0x00731140: Query digital flat-panel information and capability flags for a display, including supported UHBR modes.
0x00731142: Query DisplayPort dongle capability/attachment/type flags and maximum TMDS clock for a selected digital display.
0x00731144: Supply ELD audio capability bytes, buffer length and audio/control metadata for a display receiver. This configures display audio; it is not a CUDA channel command.
0x0073114e: Update selected entries in RM's dynamic digital-panel cache: head, HDCP capability/status and receiver identifiers, with reset/update masks.
0x00731150: Enable or disable digital-display audio for a subdevice/display; disabling stops audio and timestamp packets on the corresponding path.
0x00731152: Assign serial output resources (SORs) to displays under crossbar/link constraints, exclusions and sharing flags. This is stateful display-resource allocation.
0x00731341: Perform a DisplayPort AUX or I2C-over-AUX transaction. Inputs include display, command, address and data/length; outputs include reply type and retry information. This is physical-display communication, not a safe generic passthrough primitive.
0x00731343: Perform DisplayPort link-control operations selected by command/data and flags, including training/link configuration. Error and retry-time fields describe the result.
0x00731359: Set DisplayPort audio-stream muting mode (off/on/automatic) for the selected display.
0x00731360: Read current DisplayPort link configuration: lane count, link bandwidth (including DP2 representation) and FEC state.
0x00731362: Configure a DisplayPort stream: head/SOR/link, SST/MST selection, blanking/color settings and bandwidth/time-slot/transfer-unit parameters. This changes stream state.
0x00731378: Program stereo and selected main-stream-attribute (MSA) properties using feature masks/values and stereo enable/phase flags, independently of the normal supervisor-interrupt handling.
0x00731381: Extended MSA-property control, including feature masks/values, caching until a modeset and debug/readback fields. Exact behavior is selected by its input flags.
0x00800294: Return device brand capability bits (for example Quadro/NVS/Titan categories), not the device's numeric chip identity.
0x0080170e: For an input engine ID, return latency-buffer sizes: GPFIFO entries and pushbuffer entries (32-byte rows). OGKM includes a vGPU implementation that reads cached per-engine values; that does not establish a universal sizing formula.
0x0080170f: Set a selected channel property. Inputs are channel handle, property selector and 64-bit value. Selectors include scheduling/context-related settings; identifying the command alone does not implement every property.
0x00801812: Set the device's default virtual address space using hVASpace, subject to ownership/lifecycle checks. The public symbol omits _CMD_, which is why the earlier narrower name search missed it.
0x20800102: Query GPU information through a count and fixed array of index/data pairs. Each index has its own semantics; matching this outer layout does not imply every Windows index is supported.
0x2080012b: Promote/bind supplied engine-context resources for a selected client/channel using context-buffer descriptors, flags and routing information. This changes context state; it is also nested in four deferred requests here.
0x2080012d: Initialize a virtual engine context whose storage the caller has already cleared. Inputs identify engine/client/channel or group, virtual-memory handle or size, physical address/attributes and DMA handle/offset. The preserve flag permits rebinding an already initialized context. Seen only inside four deferred wrappers here; acceptance is not proof of later execution.
0x2080012f: Query per-unit ECC state: support/enabled/scrub status, correctable and uncorrectable counters, plus aggregate fatal-poison/error indications. Flags and GR routing identify the requested context.
0x2080014b: Read the version of a selected InfoROM object. Input is the object selector; output is its version data. A missing board object can legitimately return OBJECT_NOT_FOUND.
0x20800156: Read the InfoROM image version string. This describes board nonvolatile metadata rather than driver or GSP firmware version.
0x20800157: Query whether InfoROM ECC support exists. No parameter block; the return status carries the answer (including NOT_SUPPORTED).
0x208001a4: Read chip identity details, including PCI device ID, chip SKU and VBIOS chip revision fields.
0x20800a38: Read whether FECS context-switch hardware tracing is enabled for the selected GR route. The boolean is an output; this is GET, not the neighboring SET operation.
0x20800a9a: Request/update an internal performance boost with flags and duration. This changes boost policy; it is not simply a clock-frequency query.
0x20800af0: Notify internal display handling that the ACPI subsystem is active. The public declaration has no parameter block; the source name establishes the notification, not a complete firmware algorithm.
0x20800af1: Internal display pre-modeset notification, with no parameter block. Signals the phase before a mode transition; firmware-side details are not published here.
0x20800af2: Internal display post-modeset notification, with no parameter block. Signals the phase after a mode transition; firmware-side details are not published here.
0x20800aff: Set polling of selected RM user-shared-data fields, using a data mask and requested polling interval in milliseconds. It changes telemetry update policy.
0x2080110b: Disable or alter scheduling for a list of client/channel handles, with scheduling-only, rewind and runlist-preemption options. This is stateful channel management, not evidence of the channel's pushbuffer contents.
0x20801208: Bind ZCULL context-switch storage to a client/channel using its GPU virtual address and ZCULL mode.
0x20801211: Bind graphics/compute preemption context resources: client/channel, flags, graphics/compute modes, GR route and memory addresses for the main/spill/pagepool/beta/RTV and context-pool/control buffers. Resource sizes and correct state transitions still need implementation.
0x2080121f: Kernel-caller query: input maxSlots (nonzero); outputs slotStride, control-structure size/alignment and graphics preemption-pool size/alignment. The public 40-byte layout and field meanings are known; the sizing algorithm and per-die results are not established. Absent from this retained capture.
0x20801303: Query framebuffer/memory information via a count and index/data array. Different indices request different facts; the original Windows run exposed an unsupported index despite the known outer command.
0x20801322: Read offlined memory pages and associated source/status information. This reports memory retirement, not the ordinary GPU page-table mappings of an application.
0x20801344: Read remapped memory-row records and pending/failure flags. These are board reliability/remapping records, not a virtual-memory map operation.
0x20801347: Read the row-remapper histogram: bank counts grouped by remaining remapping capacity/usage. Values depend on hardware support and current board state.
0x20801357: Query InfoROM support/state for DRAM encryption. The returned enum distinguishes supported configurations and absent support; NOT_SUPPORTED is a legitimate result on some boards.
0x20801813: Read selected PCIe error/event counters, selected by counter mask. Returned telemetry must reflect the applicable link and hardware.
0x20801819: Read selected PCIe utilization counters, such as transmitted/received traffic and link-state residency, through a selection mask and returned counter fields.
0x20801823: Query bus information via a count and index/data array. Index-specific meaning matters; the earlier Windows failure included an unsupported index in this otherwise known command.
0x20801829: Query PCIe requester atomic-operation capabilities for a selected capability type and, where relevant, peer PCI address. Returns a capability bitmask.
0x20801830: Read PCIe completer atomic-operation capability bits.
0x20802a08: Return the required copy-engine fault-method-buffer size in bytes, used when allocating channel fault-handling resources.
0x20803083: Query NVLink platform-placement metadata: GUIDs and rack/slot/node/compute placement. This is topology information, not an NVLink transfer submission.
0x20803400: Read client-visible ECC counters for supported memory/hardware units. Which counters are meaningful depends on the device's ECC capabilities.
0x20803401: Read volatile SRAM/DRAM error counts, including SRAM parity/SECDED and DRAM correctable/uncorrectable totals. These are telemetry since the relevant reset interval.
0x20803404: Read whether TPC or channel repair is pending, as two boolean status fields.
0x20808159: Public semantic definition unresolved. Kayfabe has an empirical identity-reply rule for a 332-byte request from Linux evidence; an unchanged reply does not establish that the native call has no side effects. [Kayfabe empirical evidence](https://github.com/reindertpelsma/kayfabe/blob/c50fad9ac485f53d45d4ea77a21cb7206267c65a/crates/kf-abi/src/gsslegacy.rs).
0x20809001: Public semantic definition unresolved. Kayfabe returns a captured 8-byte pair (0x03fc007f, 0); the Windows replies agree in this capture. A matching constant is not a cross-die semantic specification. [Kayfabe empirical evidence](https://github.com/reindertpelsma/kayfabe/blob/c50fad9ac485f53d45d4ea77a21cb7206267c65a/crates/kf-abi/src/cudartinit.rs).
0x2080a026: Partially characterized empirical maximum-clock query (532 bytes), without a recovered public structure. Windows selectors differ from the existing Linux-derived input gate, so its cached authored answer cannot be assumed valid. [Kayfabe empirical evidence](https://github.com/reindertpelsma/kayfabe/blob/c50fad9ac485f53d45d4ea77a21cb7206267c65a/crates/kf-abi/src/gssreplay.rs).
0x2080a028: Partially characterized empirical per-domain clock query (2192 bytes), without a recovered public structure. Windows asks for ten domains and varies selectors; the current Linux-derived gate expects one domain. [Kayfabe empirical evidence](https://github.com/reindertpelsma/kayfabe/blob/c50fad9ac485f53d45d4ea77a21cb7206267c65a/crates/kf-abi/src/gssreplay.rs).
0x2080a084: Opaque 4-byte query observed before Linux runtime clock queries. Request/reply zero matches Kayfabe's empirical gate, but its semantic purpose remains unresolved. [Kayfabe empirical evidence](https://github.com/reindertpelsma/kayfabe/blob/c50fad9ac485f53d45d4ea77a21cb7206267c65a/crates/kf-abi/src/gssreplay.rs).
0x20810108: Opaque BinAPI operation. Earlier Linux poison-buffer experiments showed only selected output bytes changed, so it cannot be classified as a no-op. Public field meanings and the state transition remain unresolved. [Kayfabe empirical evidence](https://github.com/reindertpelsma/kayfabe/blob/c50fad9ac485f53d45d4ea77a21cb7206267c65a/crates/kf-abi/src/versions.rs).
0x50800101: Register a deferred API call: target handle, nested command, flags and client/device VA-space handles surround a payload union. Here it contains INITIALIZE_CTX or PROMOTE_CTX. Wrapper success means acceptance; later deferred execution/completion is a separate event.
0x90e70113: Query the last InfoROM black-box flush timestamp and duration in microseconds. NOT_READY can mean no flush yet; NOT_SUPPORTED can mean the board lacks the feature.
0x90f10106: Pin/reserve page-directory coverage and mirror client page-table levels in server RM. Inputs describe the subdevice, VA interval, page size and per-level physical address/size/aperture/shift. This publishes address-space state, not a general data copy.
0xa06c0101: Schedule or deschedule a channel group (TSG) using bEnable, bSkipSubmit and bSkipEnable. This changes enable/runlist state; it does not contain GPU methods.
0xa06c0103: Set a channel group's timeslice in microseconds. Hardware may round the value down; the change is immediate and can force the channel off the GPU.
0xa06c010a: Promote fault-method-buffer descriptors for the channel group/runqueues, including memory/aperture/address information. This is context-resource setup; zero-sized descriptors can be used for teardown as specified by the SDK.
0xa06f0103: Schedule or deschedule a GPFIFO channel using bEnable, bSkipSubmit and bSkipEnable. This changes enable/runlist state; it does not contain the GPU methods fetched from the ring.
0xc3700104: Query display-channel state for a hardware class/instance, including whether methods remain pending. This allows mode validation after methods propagate without itself committing an armed display state.
0xc3720101: Validate whether a proposed display mode is possible using the supplied head/window/timing configuration and resource constraints. This asks about display assembly state; it is not a graphics-engine kernel launch.
